item.title: About
item.description:
I am Trinidad Marroquin, an SRE / DevOps engineer focused on reliable infrastructure and practical automation.

I work across the parts of the stack where build systems, deployment pipelines, clusters, and production operations meet. My day-to-day interests include Kubernetes, Terraform, Packer, Rancher, Concourse, observability, Linux systems, and the process work needed to keep infrastructure understandable over time.

I value systems that are simple enough to debug under pressure. That usually means clear ownership, reproducible builds, versioned infrastructure, useful alerts, and runbooks that explain the actual operating model.

item.title: Projects
item.description:
These are starter areas for project writeups. Each project should explain the problem, constraints, design choices, and what changed operationally.

Kubernetes Platform Operations

Work around keeping Kubernetes clusters maintainable: upgrades, node lifecycle, add-on management, access patterns, backup and restore expectations, and production readiness checks.

Good writeup topics:

  • Cluster upgrade notes and rollback planning.
  • Rancher-managed fleet organization.
  • Standard namespace, ingress, storage, and policy conventions.
  • Operational checklists for new clusters.

Terraform Infrastructure Modules

Reusable Terraform patterns for infrastructure that needs to be reviewed, promoted, and changed safely.

item.title: Why This Site Exists
item.description:
This site is a place for practical notes about running infrastructure.

Most engineering writing is more useful when it includes constraints. What was the system supposed to do? What failed? What tradeoff was acceptable at the time? What would be done differently after operating it for a while?

That is the kind of writing I want to keep here.

Topics will likely include Kubernetes, Terraform, Packer, Rancher, Concourse, observability, incident response, and the small habits that make production systems easier to change. The goal is not to make infrastructure sound exciting. The goal is to make it reliable, explainable, and easier to operate.
